title: Blessed is Ram Das
hook: the minstrels Satta and Balvand praise the Gurus' light passing on (Ramkali ki Var, ang 968)
tomorrow: I never knew what You did

segments.voice: Yesterday, hukam, the divine order behind every name, and your line: many names, one lord. Today, a song by two musicians about one light in many lamps.

Open the Guru Granth Sahib and you find the Gurus' hymns, and the words of saints the Gurus gathered. But a few pages come from people who were in the room with the Gurus. Among them, tradition says, were two musicians of the Guru's court, Satta and Balvand, who played the rabab and sang. They watched the line of Gurus pass from one to the next, and they wrote about it the way musicians would: in a ballad, a var.
screen: `HYMNS BY GURUS AND SAINTS.` → `AND TWO MUSICIANS IN THE ROOM.` → `A BALLAD, A VAR.`

segments.voice: Their var sits in Raag Ramkali, on Angs nine sixty-six to nine sixty-eight. It's short, and it tells one story: Guru Nanak's light passing to Guru Angad, then to Guru Amar Das, Guru Ram Das and Guru Arjan. The line everyone remembers comes early, in a stanza about Guru Angad. In paraphrase: the light is the same, the way is the same; the Master has only changed the body. Jot ohaa, jugat saae. That single phrase holds the Sikh understanding of the ten Gurus: not ten different teachers, but one light passing from lamp to lamp. Then, on Ang nine sixty-eight, the stanza for the fourth Guru opens: dhan dhan Raam Daas gur. Blessed, blessed is Guru Ram Das; the One who made you has also adorned you. The same stanza names him as one with those before him: you are Nanak, you are Lehna, you are Amar Das. Why does it matter? Because the var is a witness. Not a theologian explaining succession, but two singers close enough to see it, saying: we watched the same light move. Sikhs still sing their var, and jot ohaa jugat saae is often quoted when people speak of the Gurus as one. And the musicians' own names, Satta and Balvand, are in the Guru Granth Sahib forever. The people who carried the tune are kept in the book.
screen: `TWO MINSTRELS, ONE BALLAD.` · `ONE LIGHT, ONE WAY, A NEW BODY.` · `BLESSED, BLESSED IS RAM DAS.` · `WITNESSES, KEPT IN THE BOOK.` · then, large: `THE LIGHT PASSES ON.`

segments.voice: Think of a person you admire, and ask who taught them: a parent, a coach, a mentor, a grandmother, a book. Picture the light passing from that teacher to them, and maybe from them to you, and silently say: blessed is the one who taught them. If you pray, say Waheguru in thanks for that line of teachers.
Jot, light: the musicians Satta and Balvand's ballad about the fourth Guru says the jot is the same, the way is the same, and only the body changes.
Your line: the light passes on. One flame, many lamps. Six hundred sixty-nine days, and counting.

screen: `DAY 669 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: I NEVER KNEW WHAT YOU DID.`

fork.setup: you're one of the Gurus' musicians, watching the leadership pass to a new Guru. what does the var say you saw?
options: the same light in a new body.
fork.reveal: the light is the same, the way is the same; only the body changed. Sikhs still speak of the Gurus as one light.

original.note: Gurmukhi: light; the var says the jot, the light, passed unchanged from Guru to Guru.

trapdoor: what you thought: it's a song praising one Guru.
what it means: it's a witness that one light passed through each Guru.
what a scholar hears: Satta and Balvand's Ramkali var (Ang 966–968) states the Gurus' single light in the words of musicians who, tradition says, served at the Guru's court.
recall: a campaign of the reform movement

chat.says: Sikhs had ten Gurus. Were they ten different teachers with different ideas?
options: Sikhs say one light passed from Guru to Guru: the same light and way, only the body changed.
Yes, each Guru started fresh, keeping only the parts of earlier teaching he liked.
No, the later Gurus only repeated Guru Nanak's hymns and added none of their own.
chat.meaning: Satta and Balvand's var says jot ohaa jugat saae: the light is the same, the way is the same; the Master only changed the body.
